text: This is ArcVault, a support-request triage workflow. It takes an incoming message, identifies the issue, and routes it to the right team.
Let’s start with a customer who can’t log in. I’ll paste their message into the tester and submit it. This calls the webhook, saves the request, and queues it for analysis.

Here’s the result: a high-priority bug report, routed to Engineering. The page shows the model’s confidence, a short summary, and details such as the account URL and error code. Each extracted detail includes a source excerpt so it’s easy to check.
Now let’s look at the other four assessment examples, which were processed earlier. The audit-log export request goes to Product. It’s a feature suggestion, with low priority.

The invoice request goes to Billing. The customer reports a charge of twelve hundred and forty dollars against a monthly rate of nine hundred and eighty. The apparent difference is two hundred and sixty dollars. That calculation happens in Python, and the assumptions are available here because the message doesn’t specify every billing detail.
The Okta message is a technical question, so it goes to Technical Support.

The dashboard outage needs a different response. Multiple users are affected, so the escalation rule sends it to Human Review. Engineering remains the standard destination, and the reason for escalation is shown immediately.
The model handles classification, extraction, and summarization in one request. Routing and escalation follow explicit Python rules, including a fallback when confidence is below seventy percent.
Every completed request has a saved JSON record containing the analysis, routing decision, and processing details. It can be exported directly from this page.
Finally, the Human Review queue brings the flagged requests together. That’s the complete flow: from an unstructured customer message to a saved, actionable result.
